shouldFix.title: The entry calls the D-086 successor 'owed' twice while creating no obligation, and the only instrument that says it is owed binds NOTHING
shouldFix.finding: The header refuses to 'perform the owed D-086 successor' and Decision item 3 repeats 'the owed D-086 successor that would name riding NT classes at G20/G21'. Calling an act owed in an adopted decision asserts that an obligation exists. Measured, none does. The obligation is described only in v6's owedLater block, and v6 is recorded here as a candidate that, in this entry's own words, 'binds NOTHING'. Nothing else creates it: no D-G* cell, no D-086 clause, and no prior COORD entry names a D-086 successor for DR-133. The sibling practice in the branch this entry cites is explicit about this. D-136 created its obligation in terms — 'Owed later MF-6: update DR-133's "no contract exists" clause. Not performed here.' — and D-138 did the same for the DR-131 cell, which is why D-139 could later schedule both as H1 and H2. D-137, by contrast, recorded a candidate that created no new owed act and used no owed language. This entry uses D-136's vocabulary while doing D-137's job, so a reader is told an obligation exists and cannot find the instrument that made it. The practical consequence is at the next act: whoever drafts the D-086 successor will look for its authority and find only a binds-nothing artifact.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: Nothing false is recorded about DR-133, the gates, or readiness, and the drafting authority for the next act arguably already exists under D-139's L section, which authorises drafting DR-133's leftover-design closures. The defect is that the entry asserts an obligation it does not create.
shouldFix.repair: Pick one and be explicit. Either add an owed-work clause in the branch's own form — 'Owed later work, not performed here: a D-086 successor, its own D-000 cycle, amends the DR-G20 and DR-G21 entries so the riding NT classes are named at those obligations the way D-086's G21 entry names DR-102 CC-1..CC-11; it adds no new DR-G* row and settles neither NT-3 nor NT-5' — which is the reading I think is intended and which would give the next cycle a citable basis. Or drop the word owed and say 'the D-086 successor v6 identifies', leaving the obligation uncreated and the path resting on D-139's L authorisation.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Fourteen attacks run, two landed. Custody is clean: subject 468188b9 at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 2d1254e, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree, and all six measured inputs reproduce including both reviewers' verdict files. The entry is otherwise well made. Its summary of v6 is accurate class by class — five riding, two not, gates 2 and 3 unanswered — and it keeps the conditioning clause that the riding classes ride only after a later D-086 successor names them, which is the correction my v5 blocker produced. It represents my own verdict correctly at ACCEPT 0/0 with CLAUDE-PONGJ-V6-ADV1 travelling as honesty work; the Codex half of the dual-ACCEPT claim I could not verify, since this prompt does not state it and I hashed that file without opening it. Every dispatch prohibition is refused in terms, the readiness recital matches live file 08 at 4 of 32, the do-not-unwrite list correctly names D-136, D-140 and D-142 and correctly omits D-141, and the COORD-scope refusal that went missing at D-140 and D-141 is back in both the header and Decision item 5. What blocks is a single word used twice. The entry refuses to perform 'the owed D-086 successor', but no adopted instrument makes that act owed: the obligation is described only in v6's owedLater block, and v6 is recorded here as a candidate that binds NOTHING. The branch this entry cites is explicit about the difference — D-136 and D-138 created their owed acts in terms, which is why D-139 could later schedule them, while D-137 recorded a candidate and used no owed language. This entry borrows D-136's vocabulary while doing D-137's job, so the next drafter will look for the authority and find a binds-nothing artifact. Either add the owed-work clause in the branch's own form, which I think is what was intended, or say 'the D-086 successor v6 identifies' and leave the path resting on D-139's L authorisation. The advisory is that the D-143 number collision is disclosed for the draft only, while a dispatch and a review prompt for the unsent G23 subject also sit live at that number with no verdicts; I measured them without opening them, and nothing operative turns on it.
